subject: Evals interlock + exception triage for PromptSet B rollout
messages:
From: Annie Park <annie@hawkanalytics.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Cc: Eric Zhao <ezhao@hawkanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: PromptSet B rollout — early quality hits and ask for exception path

Hi Sergio —

Quick note from our QA pass this morning: after switching to PromptSet B on our A/B bucket (~10% traffic) we saw a measurable drop in correctness for our entity extraction flows (precision down ~7pp). Attached is a CSV with sample conversations and the failures flagged by our analysts.

We run a fairly conservative acceptance bar and this is outside expected drift. We need to understand:
- Whether this aligns with what Redwood sees on rollout telemetry,
- If there's a fast rollback or exception plan (can we pin to PromptSet A for affected customers?), and
- A short mutual action plan to get guardrails in place so we can proceed with the larger rollout.

Can you loop in the right folks? We need a decision by EOD Monday.

Thanks —
Annie
Head of Product, Hawk Analytics

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Annie Park <annie@hawkanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PromptSet B rollout — early quality hits and ask for exception path

Thanks for the quick flag, Annie —

I'm looping in Marissa (PM for evals), Priyom (ops/orchestration), and Lauren (governance) to triage. Initial ask for our side: can you call out a small sample of canonical prompts we should use as canary checks? The sample CSV is great; short canonical cases help us validate root cause faster.

Plan I propose now:
1) Marissa — lead a short postmortem on these failure modes and propose an exception matrix (who gets pinned, for how long, rollback criteria).
2) Priyom — can we quickly implement a pinned fallback for Hawk's account or route affected customers to PromptSet A while we investigate?
3) Lauren — advise on acceptance gating and whether an SLA carve-out is needed during remediation.

I'll coordinate on the timeline; appreciate the sample attachments.

Sergio
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Cc: Annie Park <annie@hawkanalytics.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PromptSet B rollout — early quality hits and ask for exception path

Folks —

Thanks Annie + Sergio. I've reviewed the samples; high-level notes:
- Failure patterns look concentrated on short-context entity cases (dates and org names).
- Possible causes: tokenization/normalization mismatch in the new prompts, or a subtle calibration change in the verifier.

Proposed short action items (48–72h):
- A1 (Immediate canary): Create a 0.5% traffic canary for Hawk with PromptSet B + extra logging; run for 12h to capture full KV-cache behavior.
- A2 (Pin/fallback): Priyom, can you stage a per-account routing rule so we can pin Hawk to PromptSet A instantly if we detect >5% regression over 1h?
- A3 (Acceptance window): Lauren, recommend a temporary acceptance threshold override: allow Hawk to remain on A if regression >3pp for production-impacting intents until mitigations land.
- A4 (Root cause): Vivek/Vivek's team to run a focused eval comparing tokenization and verifier outputs on the failing set (I only have Marissa's laptop, but please run at scale).

I'll draft an exception matrix and share an editable spreadsheet (attaching a proposed-exception-matrix.xlsx). If we can lock in A1/A2 by EOD Monday, that should buy enough time for A4.

Marissa
Senior Product Manager, Evals

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Cc: Annie Park <annie@hawkanalytics.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 07:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PromptSet B rollout — short ops feasibility note

Quick ops note —

We have a per-account routing flag that can be applied within 30–90 minutes for emergency pinning (no code deploy). Two quick implementation options:
- Option 1 (fast): Pin Hawk to PromptSet A via routing flag; monitor traffic and lift flag after regression subsides. (Low risk, immediate)
- Option 2 (safer): Route 100% of Hawk's affected endpoints to a dedicated small canary pool running PromptSet B with enhanced logging and rollback triggers (this needs a 2–4 hour config window).

I recommend Option 1 as the immediate step and Option 2 to gather richer telemetry for the root cause. We'll need an owner to hit the rollback trigger if the 1h window crosses the 5% regression threshold.

Priyom
Platform Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PromptSet B rollout — quick technical readout

Quick technical readout from the eval team —

I ran a focused diff on the failing samples this morning. Early findings:
- The verifier score distribution shifted for short prompts; median confidence decreased by ~0.12 for the failing intents.
- Tokenization differences only explain a subset (~30%) of cases. The rest look like decoding-calibration shifts introduced by a new prompt formatting tweak.

Immediate mitigations I can spin up:
- Re-run the failing set with PromptSet B but with strict temperature/beam control to check sensitivity.
- Produce a short regression test suite (10 canonical cases) that Priyom can wire into the per-account rollback trigger (if those cases fail, auto-pin).

Marissa — I can have the regression suite and a short technical note by EOD Sunday. Priyom — happy to collaborate on the automated trigger.

Vivek
Sr. Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
